lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Morning, Captain! Nobody sails from Anchorage without their papers.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papers means a GitHub account, and either a Copilot plan or your own model provider.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: That's the New page, where new work starts. You can change your theme any time in Settings.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Hints are my job, Captain. Decisions are yours.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Ahoy, Captain! Up here! I'm Wingman, your parrot and first mate.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Every island out here teaches a chapter of the GitHub Copilot app for Beginners course, and each one has a Seal to earn.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: We're on Anchorage Cay, where you'll set up the app. Nell's by the harbourmaster's door, so start with her.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Your tasks are in the top left. If you get stuck, press Q, and I'll give you a hint.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Right, I'll ride on your shoulder. Hints are my job. Decisions are yours!

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Welcome back, Captain! Your next task's in the top left.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: If the sign doesn't name your fork, don't pull the yes lever yet.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: You'll get unlimited retries here, so try the idea that feels safest.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Quick one, Captain: those are GitHub Actions workflows. The Clock Tower’s Automations are something else, saved agent tasks, and you’ll learn those much later.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Mill’s dry today, Captain. Come back once Bo’s checked your gear.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: You’re the captain with the new fork? Suri Okoye. I keep the mill.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: This part happens on GitHub.com, not in the app. Open your fork and go to the Actions tab.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: You’ll see “Workflows aren’t being run on this forked repository.” New forks switch GitHub Actions off.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Turn them on, so GitHub can run the automated checks for your practice exercises.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Here the gate’s your Actions tab. Pull the lever, then turn the channels with E until the spring reaches my wheel.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Lever first, then turn the channels. Follow the water from the spring.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Hear that wheel sing? Your practice checks can run now. Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: There. The practice checks can run on your fork now.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Last job before the Trial: Pim and Pol run the crane on the pier head. They'll add the course's practice items to your fork.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Crane’s ready when you are, Captain.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Not yet, Captain. Our crane adds the course's practice items to your fork, and GitHub Actions has to be on first. Suri at the mill can help.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: I'm Pim, and that's Pol. Once your fork's workflows are on, we'll load it with practice issues and pull requests.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: The crane's all set, Captain. Come up whenever you're ready.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Turn the capstan, pull Dry-Run, and read the Repository line before anything else.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Preview first, always. Then --yes, but only on your own fork.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Nine pennants, five notices, seven hulls, three seals. Your fork's ready for practice!

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Remember: --dry-run first, check the Repository line, then --yes.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Captain! I'm Pim, that's Pol. We add the course's practice items to new forks.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: The course has a setup script. It adds labels, the coloured pennants, and issues, the bounty notices.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Practice branches too, the practice hulls. The bugs stay on those, never on main.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: And pull requests, sealed inspection requests: changes to review, a feedback comment, and a check that fails on purpose.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: They’re training scenarios, not problems with your setup.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Our crane works like the script. Turn the capstan to aim her, pull Dry-Run to preview, and read the Repository line on her sign.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Only when it names your own fork do you pull --yes.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Setup complete. Your fork has everything the course needs, Captain.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: In the real course you run both commands in the app’s Terminal tab, from the repository root.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Your fork's got its practice issues and pull requests now. You'll work through them in later chapters.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: The Harbormaster’s Trial waits at the lighthouse when you’re ready.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Hear that pawl? The script stops before changing a repository owned by an organization.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: There’s an --allow-shared-repository flag for that, used with --yes. Only when you’re authorized and the Repository line is exactly the target you meant.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Not today, though. Aim for your own ship.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Refused! That’s another captain’s fork. The script won’t change a repository you don’t own.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: This is the GitHub Copilot app. It's where you'll give Copilot's agents their orders and check their work.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: First things first: download and install the GitHub Copilot app for your system.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: I've put that page in your Logbook, download link and all. Press J whenever you need it, and every page you find ends up there too.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Once it's installed, open it and select Sign in to GitHub. If your company's account lives on GHE.com, choose Sign in to GitHub Enterprise Cloud instead.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: On Copilot Business or Enterprise, your organization has to switch on the GitHub Copilot app policy first.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: At Connect your repositories, carry on without adding one. You’ll connect your fork shortly.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Then the app asks you to pick a theme. Here, you pick your sails. The palette stand’s right by my door.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: The chest’s right beside my door, Captain.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papers in order. Off you go!

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Get your papers from Nell first, Captain. Then we’ll talk charts.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Every captain needs their own chart. Fork the course repository on GitHub, so your practice work lands in your own copy.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Once you’ve forked it, add it to the app. Where would you start?

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: That link takes you straight to the fork page. It’s in your Logbook now, and under your task, whenever you need it.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: That plus opens this menu. Pick Add GitHub repository, search for copilot-app-for-beginners, and select your fork. The app clones it and adds it to the sidebar.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Mind the search, though. The original course can show up right beside your fork.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Bo, the quartermaster, will get your deck ready. You’ll find him at the storehouse.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Your project shows under Projects? Good. Select the + next to it to start a project session.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Now, the workspace selector below the prompt box. Don’t trust the checkmark, it just shows the default.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Next, your tools. Open View, then Toggle Review Panel, and pick the Terminal tab. No tab? Select + and then Terminal.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Commands run there, and every tool gets a version check. My gear rack stands in for it: compass for Git, lantern for Node.js, rope for npm, and spyglass for GitHub CLI.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Run the checks at my rack, Captain. Each one should print a version number.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Run the version checks at my rack, Captain. Each one should print a version number.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Read my ledger there on the lectern. Whose signature is on it?

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: “Command not found.” No lens, no GitHub CLI. That one’s missing.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Only install what’s missing, then check again. The chandler at the market stall keeps spare lenses.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Four checks, four versions. That's a ship I'd sail.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: One more thing. GitHub CLI has its own sign-in, separate from the app. Read my ledger, there on the lectern.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Logged in as someone-else? That’s not your signature, Captain.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Logged in as you. Deck’s ready, gear’s checked, and your signature’s your own.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: One more job before the practice work: Suri Okoye at the mill race, past the storehouse. Her wheel’s been dry since your fork arrived.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Juno, your first mate. Setup’s done, so let’s give the crew their first order.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: In the app, you’d send this to the agent from your project session:

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: “Give me an overview of the copilot-app-for-beginners course repository. Focus on the learning path and the samples/book-app-web folder.”

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: You’ve been running commands in Terminal all morning. This one’s different. It’s a request for the agent.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Two fittings on the rail, just behind me. The brass speaking tube goes up to the crew, and the iron hatch goes down to the engine room. Your call, Captain.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: It’s a request for the agent, not a command. Pick the fitting on the rail that carries it.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: The crew’s proud of you, Captain. Wherever you sail next, they’re listening.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: The crew knows the ship now. The Harbormaster’s Trial waits at the lighthouse.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Hear that? The crew’s answering.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: They’ve summed up the course, chapter by chapter, and flagged samples/book-app-web. That’s the web sample you’ll use in later exercises.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: In the app, your reply will be worded differently. Models vary, and that's fine.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Commands go to the Terminal. Requests go to the agent, through the prompt box. That’s setup done, Captain. The Harbormaster’s Trial waits at the lighthouse.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: That went to the engine room, Captain. Terminal runs commands like git --version. Requests to the agent go in the prompt box.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: That went to the engine room, Captain. Terminal runs commands, not requests.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Your first mate’s waiting by your ship, Captain. Juno’s got your first order ready.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Fine colours, Captain. Ezra the chartmaker’s expecting you.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: There's a chest there too, with the list of tools you'll need: Git, Node.js, and GitHub CLI. Open it, then paint your sails and select Finish.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Pick your sails at the palette stand, then select Finish.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: A sealed captain! Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: There you are, Captain. No ship leaves Anchorage without a name, and yours has been waiting all morning.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Fair winds to her, and to all who sail in her!

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: She suits you, Captain. Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Crew’s aboard, Captain.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Right, a quick sailing lesson. The gangway’s down now, so walk up it to take the helm. W and S trim the sails, and A and D steer.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: The compass up top points back to the pier. Bring her alongside and press E, and I’ll help you dock.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Port Meridian’s east on the chart, but she’s not ready for visitors yet. Until she is, these waters are yours.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Every island has a song, Captain. Come back once your crew’s heard your first words, and I’ll play you this one.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Ah, the new captain. Sit a moment. The course you’re sailing has a song running through it: a recording studio.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Before you record anything, you get the studio ready. You sign in, plug in your gear, load the song, and run a quick soundcheck.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: You’ve just done the sailor’s version: papers signed, the chart forked, your own deck, and a first word to your crew.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Next comes Port Meridian, where you’ll learn why the app matters and tour its rooms. I’ll travel on ahead.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Fair winds, Captain. Meridian’s plaza has the best acoustics in the isles.
